help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The guests arrived after the speech had begun.

help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The preposition wegen unpacks into the conjunction weil, which opens a clause with the verb at the end.
help.tips[0].en.text: die Verschiebung des Termins wegen Krankheit des Referenten → Der Termin wurde verschoben, weil der Referent krank war.
help.tips[0].en.title: Unpack: preposition → conjunction, genitive → subject
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The rules are to be observed.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The city has raised rents sharply. → the sharp increase in rents by the city
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The verb becomes a noun (Anstieg), the subject a genitive, and the adverb a declined adjective: der deutliche Anstieg.
help.tips[1].en.text: Die Firma reagierte schnell, deshalb blieb der Schaden klein. → Dank der schnellen Reaktion der Firma blieb der Schaden klein.
help.tips[1].en.title: Pack: verb → noun, subject → genitive
help.hookEn: Turn dense official noun phrases into plain spoken sentences and back again, out loud, in about three minutes.
help.introEn: A three-minute checkpoint on the first half of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: packing and unpacking. The tutor gives you six items, one at a time. For three of them you get a dense nominal phrase (die Verschiebung des Termins wegen Krankheit des Referenten) and say it as a full sentence with the matching conjunction; for the other three you get a sentence and pack it into one nominal phrase with the right preposition and the genitive, or into a passive substitute (sein + zu, sich lassen). It listens for the conjunction or preposition that matches, the case inside the phrase, and the register. One item, one answer; say 'Ende' if you need to stop early.
help.rememberEn[0]: Unpack: wegen → weil, nach → nachdem, genitive → subject.
help.rememberEn[1]: Pack: verb → -ung noun; subject → genitive; adverb → adjective.
